subject: Post-call: PoC trial plan & deployment mode preference (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@vertex.com>, Carlos Mendes <carlos.mendes@vertex.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: PoC trial plan & deployment mode preference (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Thanks again for taking the call this morning — quick recap and proposed next steps.

Key points from discovery:
- Primary success criteria: 99th percentile inference latency under 120ms for customer-facing chat flows; <=$0.003 per 1k tokens target for steady-state cost.
- Data/classification constraints: PCI data redaction required for some payloads; Vertex requires customer-managed keys and audit logs.
- Traffic profile: bursty spikes (marketing events) with sustained baseline of ~50 concurrent users per region.

Deployment mode considerations we discussed:
- Hosted API: fastest to ship, Redwood-managed keys, lower friction for the PoC but limited to Redwood KMS (we can discuss bring-your-own-key options).
- Dedicated capacity: predictable throughput and isolation; good fit if you want committed latency and reserved GPUs.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): meets the strictest compliance requirements (KMS/HSM integration, VPC peering), longer setup time.

Proposed PoC trial plan (week-by-week):
Week 0: Kickoff + environment signoff (decide Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
Week 1: Baseline integration + sample prompts + telemetry hooks (traces/cost)
Week 2: Performance testing (throughput + 99th pct latency) + scale scenarios
Week 3: Security & compliance validation (KMS, audit logs, network topology)
Week 4: Final acceptance run + success criteria review

Attachments: PoC checklist (high level milestones & required accesses).

Ask: Can you confirm which deployment mode Vertex prefers for the trial (Hosted API, Dedicated, or Private VPC)? Also please confirm the procurement/contact who will own the contract for Dedicated or Private if we go that route.

If Hosted is acceptable for the PoC we can start next week; Dedicated/Private will need a short infrastructure alignment with your cloud/security teams (we estimate 2–3 weeks of prep for Dedicated, 4+ weeks for Private).

Happy to hop on a 30m follow-up — I’ve penciled in Tue/Wed next week as options.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Emily Park <emily.park@vertex.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, procurement@vertex.com
Date: Fri, 11 Apr 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: PoC trial plan & deployment mode preference (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Thanks Jonas — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Compliance: Vertex needs customer-managed keys and immutable audit logs for the production integration. For the PoC we can accept a simulated keys workflow, but security will want to validate KMS integration before acceptance. This leans us toward Dedicated or Private.

2) Timeline: Procurement is tracking a Q2 approval window; if the PoC requires Dedicated/Private procurement we need a formal SOW and a procurement contact. I’ve CC’d procurement@vertex.com for visibility.

3) Stakeholders: Myself (Product), Carlos Mendes (SRE), and Michael Tran (Security). Carlos will run the performance test; Michael will validate audit/KMS requirements.

Quick ask: can you share the minimal evidence we can use for security review (SOC2 scope, KMS architecture diagram, encryption-at-rest details)? Also any estimate for how long Dedicated capacity provisioning typically takes vs Private (VPC peering + DNS)?

If Hosted can be run with a stubbed KMS for the PoC and we can finalize keys for production, we’d consider Hosted for initial performance validation. But if your Dedicated setup can be reserved quickly that may be preferable.

Emily

Date: Sat, 12 Apr 2025 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: PoC trial plan & deployment mode preference (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

Appreciate the detail, Emily — answers and next actions below.

Security evidence for procurement/security review (we’ll deliver these as short artifacts):
- SOC 2 Type II summary (scoped to inference platform)
- KMS integration doc + architecture diagram (shows BYOK flow and HSM options)
- Audit log export sample + retention options (Cloud logging + long-term export)

Timing estimates (typical):
- Hosted API: immediate for PoC (hours to get API keys + telemetry).
- Dedicated capacity: provisioning and reserved pool setup typically 7–14 business days once SOW signed and infra details provided.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): 3–6 weeks depending on VPC peering, firewall rules, and HSM integration.

PoC tweak (to reduce time to validation):
- Option A (fast): Run PoC on Hosted but with a stubbed BYOK flow and synthetic audit exports. This validates latency/cost quickly while security reviews the artifacts.
- Option B (compliant): Provision Dedicated with customer-managed KMS — higher confidence for compliance but +2 weeks prep.

Proposed success criteria (concrete):
1) Performance: 99th percentile latency <= 120ms on target production prompt set during a 1-hour stress window at 2x expected peak traffic.
2) Cost: steady-state inference cost <= $0.003 per 1k tokens (within 20% tolerance).
3) Security: KMS flow validated (or for Hosted stub, security confirms artifacts are acceptable for PoC); audit logs delivered and parsable.
4) Integration: SDK-based integration + sample telemetry route returning traces to your APM.

Next steps I’ll take this week:
- Attach the SOC2 summary, KMS architecture diagram, and a short Dedicated provisioning checklist.
- Draft SOW outline (attached) for Dedicated/Private options so procurement can review.

Emily / Carlos — if you’re OK I’ll schedule the PoC kickoff for Tue Apr 22 (Hosted) or Tue May 6 (Dedicated prep). Which do you prefer?

Thanks,
Jonas

--

Summary: Vertex is leaning Dedicated for compliance, but they may accept Hosted for an initial latency/cost validation if we provide stubbed KMS artifacts. Procurement is looped; primary external contacts are Emily (Product) and Carlos (SRE).

Action items:
- Monica: own SOW + procurement communication. Target: share SOW v1 with procurement@vertex.com by Thu Apr 17.
- Aditya: validate Dedicated provisioning checklist and confirm GPU SKU options and estimated throughput for the test. Also prepare the simple BYOK stub flow (for Hosted option).
- Jonas: deliver SOC2 summary, KMS architecture, and schedule Kickoff once Monica confirms SOW cadence.

Risks & notes:
- If they go Private, plan + timeline extend significantly; escalate to AE leadership only if they require on-prem HSMs.
- Cost target tight; Aditya please include expected cost ranges for Dedicated baseline and for a 2x peak stress run.

I’ll book a 30m internal prep tomorrow 10:00 AM PST to run through the SOW and test scripts.
